messages:
alex: FYI noticed a p99 bump after the kernel selector tweak shipped to canary. Looks related to KV cache pressure + workspace churn.
perf-ci: CI alert: +3.7% p99 latency on g5n-xlarge for text-generation workloads (rolling window over last 12h).
alex: Reproduced locally on a mixed-batch trace. Reproduction steps: run trace with --profile-kv and --trace-batches.
ryan: Can you paste the profiler dump? Curious if it's allocation stalls or extra memcpy on decode path.
marta: quick dump (trimmed):
```
KVCache: total=4096MB used=3180MB free=916MB free_frag=420MB slabs=24 slab_size=256MB
Workspace: active=1.1GB peak=1.7GB recycler_reused=12% allocs/sec=240
KernelSelector: chosen=fast_attention_v2 for short-seq; fallback=matmul for long
DecodePath: avg_decode_time/token=6.8ms (+9%)
```
katie: free_frag=420MB is pretty high given only 24 slabs. That suggests fragmentation across slab boundaries when we prefill many KV entries for short contexts.
alex: Exactly. The kernel change reduced per-token compute but increased prefills per request which bloats kv and splits slabs, making recycler less effective.
ryan: So tradeoff: prefill-heavy workloads win compute but lose memory compaction. We need measured knobs: prefill cap per-request, per-model slab allocation policy, and recycler aggressiveness.
sam: Quick experiment: reduced prefill cap from 256 to 128 tokens per-request and re-ran. Result: 
```
p99 delta = -1.4% (recovery)
peak workspace = -220MB
recycler_reused = 37%
throughput = -0.6% (acceptable)
```
marta: Nice. That supports tactic A: lower prefill cap for small-sequence-heavy RLHF style traces.
alex: Another angle: improve buffer reuse by expanding recycler bucket for 256MB slab -> 384MB transient buffer so large contiguous KV chunks have place. That reduces fragmentation but ups reserved memory slightly.
katie: We should benchmark allocator changes before rollout. Small expansion might hurt multi-tenant nodes. Could gate by node-type label (dedicated vs shared).
ryan: Also saw a subtle perf regression when kernel selector used fallback matmul on trimmed sequences — extra memcpy into workspace. Maybe we need a fast path that decodes directly into KV buffer without intermediate copy.
marta: Code snippet for a potential opt:
```
// pseudo
if (decoder_can_write_directly_to_kv) {
  decoder.output_ptr = kv.slab_write_ptr();
  decode_fn(output_ptr, ...);
} else {
  decode_fn(tmp_buf, ...);
  memcpy(kv.slab_write_ptr(), tmp_buf, len);
}
```
sam: That eliminates a memcpy per decode for compatible kernels. Should measure on large-batch traces.
alex: Action items: 1) Ryan + Marta to run allocator expansion A/B on shared/capacity nodes with representative traces this afternoon. 2) Katie to add per-request prefill cap toggle and config flag with default tuned down for short-seq models. 3) Sam to prototype direct-decode path and profile memcpy win. 4) I'll prepare a canary rollout plan: opt-in per-region and slow ramp.
katie: I'll add the config flag in runtime config; default 128, ramp to 256 if recycler_reused >=30% and free_frag <200MB.
ryan: For eviction policy, suggestion: segmented LRU where prefill-created entries are in a separate segment with lower TTL and higher eviction priority. That keeps decode-cached prefixes safer.
marta: Agreed. Also add instrumentation: record eviction reasons (prefill_evicted vs decode_evicted) so we can tune TTLs.
sam: CI note: add a perf test that runs a mixed profile (prefill heavy + long decode) to detect regressions early.
alex: Great. If we see recycler_reused jump and free_frag drop in canary, we roll kernel selector to default. Otherwise rollback.
ryan: I'll kick off the runs and post raw profiler outputs here when done.
katie: thx — I'll queue the config change.
alex: :thumbsup:
perf-ci: CI job queued: perf/inference/kv-frag-mixed-trace — ETA 45m.
